examShortTricks: Trick 1: Werner's postulates: two valencies — primary (ionisable, satisfied by anions) and secondary (coordination, satisfied by ligands); test with AgCl precipitation counts (one vs three Cl− outside the sphere).

Trick 2: Nomenclature order: ligands (alphabetical, di/tri/tetra) → metal → oxidation state in Roman numerals → anion last; anionic ligands end in −o (chlorido, cyanido); neutral ligands keep names (aqua, ammine).
Trick 3: VBT: inner-orbital (d²sp³, low spin) vs outer-orbital (sp³d², high spin) — count unpaired electrons to decide; [Fe(CN)6]³⁻ has 1 unpaired (low spin), [FeF6]³⁻ has 5 (high spin).
Trick 4: CFT: d orbitals split into t2g and eg by Δo; strong-field ligands (CN−, NH3) pair electrons; weak-field (F−, H2O) don't — spectrochemical series snippet earns the mark.
